children: The yield on the 10-year Australian Government Bond surged to over 5.17% in September, the highest since 2011, and tracking the rise in global bond yields on expectations of higher interest rates by major central banks.
The return of strikes between the US and Iran added to pessimism on energy supply from the Middle East and rekindled pro-inflationary risks in major economies.
This magnified the impact of an overshot domestic inflation print in July, when headline inflation rose to 3.6%, ahead of expectations of 3.3%.
Markets increased exposure to hedges against a incoming rate hike by the RBA after minutes from the central bank's last meeting reflected growing concerns over price growth.
Global inflation also raised bets on hikes by the Fed and BoJ this year.
On top of that, record corporate debt issuance, including Australian dollar offerings by Alphabet, also lifted yields.

title: 10-Year AGB Yield Soars to 15-Year High
